subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw implement broad configured-model probing as `models status --probe --all`, fold it into fallback-chain or staged-migration UX, or defer it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent command surface controls live provider calls, output contracts, rate-limit behavior, and overlap with other open model-diagnostics requests, so automation should not choose it alone.

options.title: Add `--probe --all` To Models Status
options.body: Implement the requested opt-in sweep while preserving default one-model-per-provider auth probing and documenting provider filtering plus JSON output.

options.title: Fold Into Fallback/Migration UX
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/6599 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/17876 own the model-verification flow and keep `models status --probe` focused on auth/profile diagnostics.

options.title: Defer Live Model Sweeps
options.body: Leave current auth probes and external/dashboard approaches in place until maintainers settle token, cost, and provider-support policy.

recommendation.title: Add `--probe --all` To Models Status
recommendation.body: Implement the requested opt-in sweep while preserving default one-model-per-provider auth probing and documenting provider filtering plus JSON output.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current auth-probe path and has the strongest combined history across model status/probe and provider-routing decisions.
